transcript.content: Hello. I'm a psychiatrist, and I'm here to help you. What brings you in to see me today?

I've been struggling with severe depression, constant sadness, and feeling completely exhausted for about two years now. Along with that, I've been experiencing some really unsettling things like hearing voices and feeling paranoid. I just really need some help because it has become too much to handle.
Have you ever experienced these unsettling things, like hearing voices or feeling paranoid, during times when your mood was relatively normal and you weren't feeling depressed?

Yes, I have. There have been times, for at least a couple of weeks, when my mood felt relatively stable and I wasn't feeling deeply depressed, but I still heard those voices and felt like I was being watched. It's really confusing because those scary experiences seem to happen even when the sadness lifts a bit.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days where you felt the opposite of depressed—like having bursts of extreme energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling unusually high or irritable?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've never had those kinds of high-energy bursts or felt unusually high. For the most part, I just feel extremely drained and down.
Looking back at the entire time you've experienced these voices or paranoia, would you say you have been severely depressed for most of that time?

Yes, looking back, I would say I've been severely depressed for the vast majority of that time. Even when the voices or paranoia seemed to change, the deep sadness, low energy, and foggy thinking have been almost constantly with me. It feels like the depression has been the main backdrop of everything I've gone through.
To help me understand everything fully, have you recently used any recreational drugs, alcohol, or new medications, or do you have any known medical conditions?
No, I don't use any recreational drugs or drink alcohol at all. I haven't started any new medications recently, and as far as I know, I don't have any medical conditions.

latest_inference.note: The patient presents with concurrent depressive and psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and paranoia) lasting for two years, with depressive symptoms present for the majority of the illness. Crucially, the patient reports experiencing these psychotic symptoms for at least two weeks in the absence of a major depressive episode, which distinguishes this from Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features. The absence of manic or hypomanic episodes rules out Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) and Bipolar I/II disorders, and the prominent, long-standing depressive symptoms rule out Schizophrenia. Thus, Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is the final diagnosis.
